title: C1164 — Cylinder head temperature (CHT) sensor connector
introduction:
I read this cylinder head temperature (CHT) sensor reference as a map of the connector’s electrical roles. The identity table describes the connector, the face drawing locates its labeled cavities, and the assignment table distinguishes the sensor circuit from the powertrain controller’s signal-return circuit. Think of them as the temperature report and its return path; the table names their jobs without proving that either circuit is working.

Start with the drawn cavity label, then read its assignment row across to the terminal information. Repeated cavity entries carry different gauge and terminal details; they do not add positions to the drawing. Use the pigtail table separately to distinguish the service assembly from its engineering shell identifier.

This page supports identification, not connector probing, wire selection, sensor testing or replacement. Physical viewing direction, gauge convention and the meanings of Size and Used remain unspecified, and signal return is not an instruction to connect the circuit to chassis ground. The summary’s pin-count entry conflicts with the drawing and pigtail cavity count; that disagreement remains unresolved.

edits.why: As displayed, the upper cavity maps to the sensor circuit and the lower cavity to signal return. I use the printed cavity labels to connect the illustration to the table. The housing projection above the cavities helps describe the drawing’s shape, but its release function and the physical viewing direction are not established.

edits.text: Read the sensor and return assignments
edits.why: Cavity links each row to the drawing, Circuit Number identifies the circuit, and Function states its role. Keep each row’s gauge and Terminal Part Number together. The repeated return-circuit rows record distinct details without establishing that their terminals are interchangeable or explaining which configuration selects each row.

The pigtail is the connector assembly with attached wire leads. Its Service Part identifies the service item, while Engineering Shell identifies the shell reference. The pigtail’s gauge and material fields are separate from the circuit-assignment details; this table does not establish a splice method or a reason to replace the connector.

originalAuthorHold: The identity table states Pin Count 3, but the connector drawing labels only cavities 1 and 2 and the pigtail table states Cavities 2. Preserve all original data and resolve this conflict before treating the summary pin count as authoritative.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all31 primary units, both complete source pages and sole figure, and3 edits. PinCount3 versus pictured1–2/kit2 and repeated RE454 gauge/terminal applicability ambiguity retained for bounded identification reading only.
